Every officer or servant of the Authority shall, before, on or after entering upon his duties under this Act, sign a declaration pledging himself to observe strict secrecy respecting all transactions of the Authority or the General Manager and all matters relating to such transactions, and shall, by such declaration, pledge himself not to reveal any matter which may come to his knowledge in the discharge of his duties except-
when required to do so by the General Manager; or
in the performance of his duties; or
in order to comply with the provisions of this Act or any other law.

Every officer or servant of the Authority shall decline to answer any question concerning the business of the Authority if he cannot answer the question without infringing his pledge of secrecy under subsection (1).

Every officer or servant who fails or refuses to sign the declaration, or to observe the pledge, referred to in subsection (I) shall be guilty of an offence and shall, on conviction after summary inquiry before a Magistrate, be liable to a fine not exceeding five hundred rupees or to imprisonment of either description for a period not exceeding six months or to both such fine and imprisonment.

The Minister may, from time to time, give the Authority general or special directions as to the exercise, discharge and performance of its powers, functions and duties under this Act and such directions shall be carried out by the Authority.

The Minister may, from time to time, direct in writing the Authority to furnish him such information with respect to the property, business and activities of the Authority, as he may require and the Authority shall carry out every such direction.
The Minister may make regulations for the purpose of carrying out or giving effect to the principles and provisions of this Act.
In particular and without prejudice to the generality of the powers conferred by subsection (1), the Minister may make regulations in respect of all or any of the following matters:
the conduct and management of the affairs of the Authority;
the control of the business transactions of the Authority;
the forms to be issued for any of the matters required under this Act;
any other matters prescribed or in respect of which regulations are authorized by this Act to be made.
Every regulation made by the Minister shall be published in the Gazette and shall come into operation on the date of such publication or on such later date as may be specified in the regulation.

Every regulation shall as soon as convenient after publication in the Gazette be brought before Parliament for approval. Any regulation which is not so approved shall be deemed to be rescinded from the date of its disapproval but without prejudice to anything previously done thereunder.
Notification of the date on which any regulation made by the Minister is deemed to be rescinded shall be published in the Gazette.

It shall be lawful for the General Manager or any officer generally or specially authorized by him in writing in that behalf, at any reasonable time, to enter upon any land or premises and then do such acts as may be reasonably necessary for the purpose of carrying out or giving effect to any work of the Authority, or of making of any survey, examination or investigation, preliminary or incidental to the exercise of any power, the discharge of any function or the performance of any duty of the Authority.
All members, officers and servants of the Authority shall be deemed to be public servants within the meaning of, and for the purposes of, the Penal Code.
The Authority shall be deemed to be a scheduled institution within the meaning of the Bribery Act, and the provisions of that Act shall be construed accordingly.
No suit or prosecution shall lie (a) against the Authority for any act which in good faith is done or purported to be done by the Authority under this Act; or
against any member, officer, servant or agent of the Authority for any act which in good faith is done or purported to be done by him under this Act or on the direction of the Authority.

Any expense incurred by the Authority in any suit or prosecution brought by or against the Authority before any court shall be paid out of the funds of the Authority, and any costs paid to, or recovered by, the Authority in any such suit or prosecution shall be credited to the Fund of the Authority.

Any expense incurred by any such person as is referred to in paragraph (A) of subsection (1) in any suit or prosecution brought against him before any court in respect of any act which is done or is purported to be done by him under this Act or on the direction of the Authority shall, if the court holds that such act was done in good faith, be paid out of the Fund of the Authority, unless such expense is recovered by him in such suit or prosecution.
The Authority may make rules in respect of all or any matters for which are authorized or required by this Act to be made.
No rule made by the Authority under this Act shall have effect until it has been approved by the Minister.
Without prejudice to the generality of the powers conferred by subsection (1), the Authority may make rules in respect of all or any of the following matters:
the form and manner in which contracts may be entered into by the Authority;
the delegation of powers to officers and servants of the Authority;
the form and manner in which the accounts of the Authority shall be maintained;
the conduct and disciplinary control of officers and servants of the Authority;
the conditions of service and the remuneration payable to officers and servants of the Authority;
the granting of loans, allowances or gratuities payable to officers and servants of the Authority;
the provision of housing accommodation for officers and servants of the Authority; and
the provision of professional and technical training of officers of the Authority.

The provisions of the laws set out in the Schedule hereto shall have no application in relation to any property, business and any activity of the authority or to any legal proceeding relating to such property, business or activity.

Every person who contravenes or, fails to comply with any provision of this Act, or of any subsidiary written law made or issued thereunder shall be guilty of an offence and shall on conviction before a Magistrate be liable to imprisonment of either description for a term not exceeding two years or to a fine not exceeding one thousand rupees or to both such imprisonment and fine.

To demand in writing (a) from the person claiming to be the owner of any land or premises, or of his agent, the production of every deed, document or other instrument upon which he claims title to such land or premises;
from the person claiming to be the owner of any land or premises, or of his agent, the production of every deed, document or other instrument upon which he claims title to such land or premises;
from the occupier of such land or premises the authority upon which he bases his occupation and information about the whereabouts of the owner of such land and premises,

and where such owner or occupier as the case may be, within ten days of such demand (i) refuses or fails without cause to produce the deed, document or other instrument upon which he bases his claim to the said land or premises .

is unable to produce such deed, document or instrument as such deed, document or other instrument is not in his possession and refuses without cause to inform or give information as to the whereabouts of the person in whose possession such deed, document or other instrument is,
such owner or occupier shall be guilty of an offence under this Act and shall be liable on conviction after summary trial before a Magistrate to a fine not exceeding ten thousand rupees

The deed, document, or other instrument demanded under section 14 shall be produced on the premises to which such deed, document or instrument may relate or at such other place as the person demanding the same may require and the power of demanding the production thereof, under section 14 shall be deemed to include the power of making such examination of such deed, document or other instrument, as shall be necessary for the purpose of a land survey, and every person refusing or failing without cause to permit such examination of any such deed, document or other instrument to any person referred to in section 14, shall be guilty of an offence under this Act and shall be liable on Conviction after summary trial before a Magistrate to a fine not exceeding ten thousand rupees.

The Surveyor-General or a registered surveyor authorised in that in writing by the Surveyor-General may after reasonable notice given to occupier enter upon any land or premises and make such inspection survey and installation of survey mark as shall be necessary to enable such Surveyor-General or survey authorised as the case may be to conduct a land survey thereon

It shall be lawful for the Surveyor-General or a registered surveyor authorised in that behalf in writing by the Surveyor-General under this Act or any other written law to conduct a land survey after such entry and to demand, from the owner or the occupier of such land or premises by notice in writing, the production of any deed, document, other instrument or plan that affects the title, or any legal interests (hereto. Such owner or occupier shall within ten days of such demand produce such deed, document, other instrument or plan to the Surveyor-General or such surveyor, as the case may be.

On the production of such deed document other instrument or plan it shall be lawful for such Surveyor-General or such surveyor to examine and make notes extracts and copies of such deed document other instrument or plan to be used for the purpose of this Act or for the purpose of any other written law.

- Where the Surveyor-General or any registered Surveyor authorised in that behalf by the Surveyor-General shall under pretence of performing any duty or exercising any power imposed of conferred on him by this Act abuses his power of uses unnecessary violence or wantonly does any injury or gives uncalled for or vexatious annoyance the Surveyor-General or such surveyor shall be guilty of an offence and shall be liable on conviction after summary trial before a Magistrate to a fine no exceeding thousand rupees

Every person who wilfully obstruct or hinders the Surveyor-General or registered Surveyor authorised by him in that behalf of a registered licensed Surveyor or any person assisting such Surveyor-General in the performance of his duties in relation to any survey or the ascertaining making out of any boundary of any survey lines, or the fixing, plating, restoring, repairing or setting up of any survey mark shall be guilty of an offence and shall on conviction after summary trial before a Magistrate, be liable to a fine not exceeding ten thousand rupees

Every person, who knowingly or wilfully removes, destroys, or after the position of or markings on any survey mark that has been placed or set up for the control of surveys or definition of boundaries or for the purpose any survey conducted under or for the purposes of this ACT OR any other written law shall be guilty of an offence and shall, on conviction after summary trial before a Magistrate, be liable to a line not exceeding ten thousand rupees

Every person, who is convicted of an offence under subsection (1) shall, in addition to the fine for which ho may be liable in respect of such offence, be also liable to pay the cost, including survey costs, and cost associated with repairing, replacing, or restoring to its proper position, any survey mark or restoring the markings on any survey mark that is the subject of the of the offence for which he is convicted which costs shall be assessed by the surveyor General and recovered if it were a fine

Every person who places in position in relation to any land any peg, mark. land mark or other mark, not being a survey mark properly placed that is intended to cause any person to believe that it is a survey or land mark placed in that position for the purposes of any survey under this Act or other written law shall be guilty of an offence and shall be on conviction after summary trial before a Magistrate be liable to a fine not exceeding twenty thousand rupees.

Any cadastral map, plan or any other plan or map prepared in accordance with the provisions of this act or any written law purported to be signed by the surveyor general or officer acting on his behalf and offered in evidence in any suit shall be received in evidence and shall be taken to be prima facie proof of the facts stated there in and shall not be necessary to prove that it was in fact signed by the surveyor General or an officer acting on his behalf, nor that it was made by his authority, nor that the same is accurate until the evidence to the contrary shall have first been given.

Any cadastral map, plan or any other plan or map prepared in accordance with any written law. Purporting to be a true copy of such a plan or map and purporting to be signed by the surveyor general or any officer acting on his behalf shall be admissible evidence in all cases and for all purposes instead of the original and may be taken as prima facie evidence of the truth of the facts stated there in as being that of the original and it shall not be necessary to prove that such copy was infact signed or authenticated by the surveyor-general or such officer nor that it is a true copy. Nor that the facts reflected there in are accurate. Until evidence to the contrary shall have first been given.

The boundaries surveyed for the preparation of a cadastral map or any plant for the purposes of the registration of titles Act shall. where it is not otherwise defined by permanent futures be defined by marks which will be referred to as land marks which landmarks shall be deemed to be State Land Marks within the meaning of the State Land Marks Ordinance.

Every occupier claimant or owner of any land or premises shall maintain without disturbing any landmarks placed on the boundary of such land or premises and any survey mark placed within such land or premises:

Provided however that in the case of any land marks placed along the boundary of reservation reserve or state land or premises belonging to the state every claimant occupier lessee or owner of land adjoining such reservation reserve or state land shall maintain without disturbing any land marks placed on such Boundary.

Every regulation made by the Minister under this section shall be published in the Gazelle and shall come into operation on the date of such publication or such later date as may be specified in the regulation.

Every regulation made under this section shall, within a period of six months from the date of its publication in the Gazette be brought before Parliament for approval. There shall be established a council which shall be called the Land Survey Council(hereinafter in this Act referred to as "the council")
The Council shall by the name assigned to it by subsection (1)be a body corporate and shall have perpetual succession and a common scale and may sue and be sued in name.
The Council shall consist of the following:-
ex-officio members namely-
the Surveyor-General who shall be the chairman;
a registered surveyor not below the rank of a Deputy Surveyor-General nominated by the Surveyor-General. who shall be the Vice-Chairman:
the Director of the institute of Surveying and Mapping established by the Institute of Surveying and Mapping Act.No.21 of 1969; and
appointed members namely:-
three registered surveyors who possess wide experience and proven capabilities in land surveying nominated by the Surveyors Institute of the SriLanka(Incorporation)Act No. 22 of 1982; and

one academic nominated by the University Grants Commission established by the Universities Act No 16 of 1978 from among academics in the fields of education administration, management of engineering from a university.
Who shall be appointed by the Minister
A person shall be disqualified from being appointed or continuing as a member of the Council -
if he is or becomes a member of parliament or a provincial council or any local authority; or
if he is not or ceases to be a citizen of Sri lanka: or
if he is under any law in force in sri lanka or in any other country found or declared to be of unsound mind:or
if he is serving or has served a sentence of imprisonment imposed by any court in Sri Lanka or any other country:or
if he has any financial or other interest as is likely to affect prejudicially the discharge by him of his functions as a member of the Council:or
if he is an undischarged bankrupt:or
if he is absent from three consecutive meetings of the council without the permission of the Council:or
if he is found guilty of an offence under this Act.
An appointed member of the Council may resign his office by letter addressed to the Minister and such resignation shall be effective from the date on which it is accepted by the Minister.
The Minister may, after consulting the authority nominating an appointed member, remove such member from office for reasons stated in writing:
where an appointed member of the Council dies resigns or is removed from office the minister shall having regard to the provisions of paragraph (b)of section 27 appoint another member in his place.
A member appointed under subsection (3) shall hold office for the unexpired part of the term of office of the member whom succeeds.
Every ex-officio member of the council shall hold office as long as he holds the post by virtue of which he is a member of the council.
Subject to the provisions of subsections(1)and(2) of section 29 the term of office of an appointed member of the Council shall be three years and such member shall be eligible for re-appointment.

The members of the Council shall be paid such renunciation or allowances out of the Fund of the Council shall rates as may be determined by the Minister in consultation with the Minister in charge of the subject of Finance.
There shall be a Secretary to the Council who shall be appointed by the Council.

The Secretary be in charge of the day to day administration of the affairs of the Council. The Secretary shall keep a record of the minutes of the meetings of the Council and shall be entitled to speak at such meetings but shall not be entitled to vote thereat.

The Chairman or in his absence the Vice-Chairman shall preside at meetings of the Council. In the absence of both the Chairman and the Vice-Chairman. a member elected by the members present shall preside at such meeting.
The Council may regulate the procedure in regard to its meetings and the transaction of business at such meetings.
The quorum for a meeting of the Council shall be four members.

All questions for decision at any meeting of the Council shall be decided by the vote of a majority of the members present, In the case of an equality of votes. The Chairman or other member presiding at that meeting of the Council shall in addition to his own vote, have, a casting vote.
No act, decision or proceedings of the Council shall be deemed to be invalid by reason only of the existence of a vacancy in the Council or any defect in the appointment of any member of the Council.
The seal of the Council may be determined and devised by the council, and may be altered in such manner as may be determined by the council
The seal of the Council shall be in the custody of the Secretary.

The seal of the Council shall not be affixed to any instrument or document except with the sanction of the Council and in the presence of the Chairman and one member who shall sign the instrument or document in token of their presence.
The Council shall maintain a register of the instruments and documents to which the seal of the Council has been affixed.
The Council may delegate any of the powers and functions of the Council to the chairman.

The Chairman to whom any of the powers and functions of the Council have been delegated under subsection (1)shall exercise and discharge such powers and functions subject to the general or special directions of the Council.
The functions of the Council shall be-
to maintain standards and procedures relating to land surveying and professional discipline among persons engaged in land surveying.

to receive applications from surveyors for registration as registered surveyors, and to register such surveyors where the Council is satisfied that such surveyors possess the prescribed qualification and experience and have the ability and skills to practise land surveying;

to receive applications from registered surveyors for the issue of an Annual Practicing licence and to issue such licences to such surveyors where the Council is satisfied that such surveyors possess the knowledge and skill to practise the profession of land surveying;
to promote the maintenance of high standards of professional education among persons engaged in land surveying;
to promote programs which provide for professional development by improving the knowledge and skills of persons practicing land surveying and who are required to obtain an Annual practicing Licence;

to recognize academic and professional qualifications in land surveying, establish practical experience requirements and conduct qualifying examinations and professional interviews, for candidates for registration surveyors and for the issue of annual practicing licenses;

to negotiate and administer reciprocal arrangements with the relevant authorities in foreign countries for the purpose of security uniformity and reciprocity in the education, training and recognition of persons engaged in land surveying;
to co-ordinate with the institutions engaged in education and training in land surveying and land information in Sri Lanka, for the maintenance of required educational standards;
to co-ordinate with other relevant organisations in Sri Lanka in the maintenance of high professional standards.
The Council shall have the power-
to acquire, hold, take or give on lease or hire,mortgage,pledge,sell or otherwise dispose of any movable or immovable property;
to accept gifts, grants or donations whether in cash or otherwise and to apply them for discharging its functions;
to appoint such officers and servants as may be necessary for carrying out the work of the Council;
to determine the remuneration payable to the officers and servants so appointed;
to appoint committees for the effective discharge of its Junctions;
to establish a social security scheme and provide welfare and recreational facilities, for its officers and servants;
to make rules in respect of the administration of the affairs of the Council; and
generally, to do all such other things as are necessary lo facilitate the proper discharge of the functions of the Council.

From or alter the date of commencement of this Act no person, other than a person who possesses the qualification specified in the Schedule hereto and has obtained registration with the Council and has been issued with a certificate of registration which is for the time being force. may engage in land surveying.

Notwithstanding the provisions of subsection (1) a person who possesses the academic qualifications specified in the Schedule hereto and working under the supervision of a person issued with a certificate of registration under subsection (1), may engage in land surveying for the purpose of acquiring the practical qualification specified in the Schedule hereto, but shall not be eligible to be registered under this Act.
An application for registration as a surveyor shall he in the prescribed form and shall be accompanied by the prescribed ice.

The Council may, on an application received in that behalf by a person engaged in or proposing to engage in land surveying and on production of evidence of good character and payment of the prescribed ice, register such person where the Council is satisfied that such person has the qualifications and experience and skills lo engage in land Surveying.

Notwithstanding the provisions of section 39.every surveyor to be issued with an annual licence under section 4 or section 6 of the Surveyors Ordinance on the date of commencement of this Act shall be deemed to be registered under this Act.
Every surveyor deemed to be registered under this Act, shall as soon as convenient submit to the Council the following particulars;-
name and address of the surveyor;
the criteria or qualification, the possession of which entitled him to be issued with an annual licence under the Surveyors Ordinance.

Every surveyor registered with the Council under subsection (3)or(4) of section 39 or deemed to be registered under subsection (1),shall be issued with a certificate of registration and shall be referred to in this Act as a "registered surveyor".
Every registered surveyor who is desirous of practicing or attempting or professing to practise land surveying, shall apply to the Council for an Annual Practicing licence;

Provided however, registered Surveyors in the Survey Department engaging in land surveying under the supervision of the Surveyor General. shall not be required to obtain an Annual Practicing licence for the purpose of engaging in land surveying on behalf of the Government.

The Council may on application received in that behalf by a registered surveyor accompanied by the prescribed fee. issue to such surveyor an Annual Practicing Licence where the Council is satisfied that he has followed the prescribed courses of study and training approved by the Council and acquired knowledge and skill to practise land surveying.

Notwithstanding the provisions of subsection (1), every registered surveyor who is engaged in land surveying on the dale of commencement of this Act may. Continue to practice land surveying for a period of six months from such dale but shall within such period apply for the Annual Practicing Licence under this Act.
Every registered surveyor issued with an Annual Practicing Licence under subsection (2) is referred to in this Act as a "registered licensed surveyor".
The Council shall maintain a register of all (a) registered surveyors; and-
registered licensed surveyors

The registers maintained under subsection (!) shall contain the names, qualifications and addresses of all registered surveyors and alt registered licensed surveyors, the respective dates on which they were registered or issued with such licences and such other particulars as may be required to be maintained under this Act.
The registers shall be open for public inspection by any person on payment of the prescribed fee.
The Council shall on payment of a prescribed Ice supply a certified copy of any entry in any register to any person requesting such copy.

The Council shall on or before the thirty first day of March in each year publish in the Gazette a list of the names of all registered licensed surveyors and shall within one month of the cancellation or suspension of an Annual Practicing Licence publish a notification giving notice thereof in the Gazette.
The Council shall where it considers it necessary to do so cause the register of the registered surveyors or part thereof to he published in the Gazette.

A copy of any entry in any such register purporting to be certified by the Chairman of the Council shall in all proceedings whatsoever be prima facie evidence that the person stated therein "(a) is a registered surveyor;
holds or does not hold an annual practicing licence as the case may he;
possesses the qualification therein stated;
has had his registration cancelled or suspended as the case may be: or
has had his Annual Practicing Licence cancelled or suspended as the case may be.
A registered surveyor (a) may engage in land surveys in the service of the Government and when authorised by the Surveyor General; or
may engage in land surveys in the service of the Government and when authorised by the Surveyor General; or
who holds a Annual Practicing License, may engage in the practice of land surveying for fee or reward.

For the purposes of this Part a registered surveyor shall be guilty of professional misconduct if he is found in any proceedings or appeal (a) to have been negligent or incompetent in the conduct of any survey;

to have failed to comply with any guidelines or directions pertaining to the practice of surveying of the requirements pertaining to the preparation of and maintenance of survey plans and cadastral maps as are prescribed;
to have certified as to the accuracy of any survey or any plan or map in relation to a survey-
where such surveyor being an officer in the service of the Government has conducted the survey of certified the plan or map without exercising due care or caution
where such surveyor being a registered licensed surveyor;
(A) has conducted such survey or certified the plan or map, without exercising due care or caution.

(B) without having personally conducted such survey, has caused it to be done by another registered licensed surveyor and has not taken sufficient measures to ensure the accuracy of the field work and office work of such other surveyor
without having personally conducted such survey, has caused it to be done by a person other than by a registered licensed surveyor.
(D)has certified to the accuracy of such survey, map or plan knowing it to be defective;
to have made any entry in any field book or other record that purports to have been derived from actual observation or measurement in the field where in fact it has not been so derived.

to have supplied to the Surveyor-General or any other registered surveyor any erroneous information in relation to any survey, survey mark, or boundary, knowing that information to be erroneous in any material particular;

to have failed, without reasonable cause, to perform any duty imposed on a registered surveyor under this Act or comply with any condition subject to which he was allowed by the Council to practise land surveying.

For the purposes of determining whether or not any registered surveyor is guilty of professional misconduct the fact that any survey plan or map may have been approved by or on behalf of the Surveyor-General shall not be relevant.-

Every charge of professional misconduct against a registered surveyor shall be reported to the Council in writing, signed by the person making the charge and if it appears to the Council that it is one into which an inquiry should be held, the Council shall fix a time and place for such inquiry.

The Council shall conduct an inquiry relating to any charge of professional misconduct against a registered surveyor, made under subsection(1) and the Council may where necessary, obtain the services of any person who is competent in the Held of land surveying or any other field to assist the Council in conducting such inquiry.

At least twenty eight days prior to the date fixed for such inquiry, notice in writing shall be sent by the Secretary to the last known postal address of such surveyor, informing him of the time and place fixed for the inquiry, and supplying him with a copy of all charges made against him.
At an inquiry held under this section -
the surveyor charged shall be entitled to be heard in his defence; and
the Council shall -
act according to equity, good conscience and the substantial merits of the case, without regard to technicalities and legal norms; and
not be bound by the rules of evidence-, but may inform itself on any matter in such manner as it thinks fit.
The decision of the Council on such inquiry shall be in writing and shall be signed by at least two members of the Council who conducted such inquiry and shall be countersigned by the Secretary.
The Council shall give reasons for its decision in respect of the inquiry.

Where the Council, after conducting an inquiry in accordance with this Part is satisfied that a registered surveyor is guilty of professional misconduct the Council may. Make one or more of the following orders:
make an order that the registration of the registered surveyor be cancelled and the name of such surveyor be removed from the register;
make an order that the registration of the registered surveyor be suspended for a period not exceeding three years;
make an order that the Annual Practising Licence issued to a registered surveyor be cancelled:
make an order that the Annual Practising Licence issued to a registered surveyor be suspended;
make an order that the registered surveyor may, for a period not exceeding three years, engage in the practice of land surveying subject to such conditions as the Council may impose;
make any other appropriate order as, to costs or otherwise as the Council considers appropriate.

While any order of suspension of registration under this section remains in force the person shall be deemed for the purpose of this Act not to be registered but forthwith on the expiry of the order his rights and privileges as a registered surveyor shall be revided as from the date of such expiry.
All costs and expenses payable under this section shall be recoverable as a debt due to the Council.
Every registered surveyor in respect of whom an inquiry is conducted under section 46,shall be to appear in be heard, either personally or by his representative at the inquiry.
Every person who is dissatisfied with-
any decision of the Council relating to an application by him for registration or the issue of an Annual Practicing Licence; or
any order of the Council under section 47 relating to him.
may,within thirty days after notice of the decision or order has been communicated to him by the Secretary, appeal to the Court of Appeal against the decision or order, as the case may be.

The Secretary shall enter in the register against the entry relating to the relevant surveyor, the fact that his registration or Annual Practicing Licence or both has or have been cancelled and any conditions imposed on him for the practise of land surveying under section 47.

Every registered surveyor whose registration or Annual Practicing Licence is cancelled or suspended under this Part of this Act shall within fourteen days after the date on which written notice of the cancellation or suspension as the case may be has been given to him. Deliver to the Secretary any certificate issued to him under this Act which has not been so delivered before that date.

Every registered surveyor who fails to comply with the provisions of subsection (1) shall be guilty of an offence under this Act and shall on conviction after summary trial before a Magistrate be liable to a fine not exceeding ten thousand rupees.

The Council may from time to time appoint committees, consisting of not more than three members of the Council and such other persons as the Council thinks fit, to inquire into and report to the Council on any matter within the scope of the functions of the Council other than the functions assigned to the Council by sections 37 and 46.
Every committee appointed under subsection (I) shall be subject in all matters to the control of the Council.
The Council shall in each year submit a report to the Minister on the discharge and performance of its functions and duties and the exercise of its powers.
A copy of such annual report shall be laid before Parliament as soon as practicable after it has been received by the Minister.

The Council may require registered surveyors to attend specified courses to gain specified experience. or to take other appropriate action. within a specified period for the purpose of maintaining and improving their knowledge and skills in the practice of land surveying.
Where the Council is satisfied that-

a registered surveyor who has been issued with an Annual Practicing Licence has not complied with any of the requirements imposed under subsection (1), the Council may (i) suspend the Annual Practicing Licence of such registered surveyor until the requirements are complied with:

renew the Annual Practicing Licence of such registered surveyor subject to specified conditions, which may include a condition specifying the standard period for which that Annual Practicing license is renewed;
refuse to renew the Annual Practicing Licence of such registered surveyor until those requirements are complied with; or

a registered surveyor who is in the service of the Government has not complied with the requirements imposed under subsection (I) the Council may report such non compliance to the Surveyor-General for appropriate action.
The Council may appoint such officers and servants as it considers necessary for the efficient discharge of its functions.

The officers and servants appointed under subsection (I) shall be remunerated in such manner and at such rates and shall he subject to such conditions of service as may be determined by the Council with the approval of the Minister.

At the request of the Council any officer in the public service may, with the consent of that officer and the Secretary to the Ministry of the Minister in charge of the subject of Public Administration,be temporarily appointed to the staff of the Council for such period as may he determined by the Council with like consent, or be permanently appointed to such staff.

Where any officer' in the public service is temporarily appointed to the staff of the Council,the pirovisions of subsection(2) of section 14 of the National Transport Commission Act. No. 37 of 1991, shall mutatis mutandis,apply to,and in relation to. him.

Where any officer in the public service is permanently appointed to the staff of the Council,the provisions of subsection (3) of section 14 of the National Transport Commission Act.No.37 of 1991, shall, mutatis, mutandis, apply to and in relation to him

Where the Council employs any person who has agreed to serve the Government for a specifiedperiod, any period of service to the Council by that person shall be regarded as service to the Government for the purpose of discharging the obligations of such agreement.
The Council shall have its own fund (hereinafter referred to as "the Fund")
There shall be paid into the Fund (a) all such sums of money as may be made available to the Council out of the Consolidated Fund:
all such sums of money as may be received by the Council in the exercise,performance and discharge of its powers and functions under this Act;and
all such sums of money as may be received by the Council by way of gifts,grants or donations.

There shall be paid out of the Fund all such sums of money as are required to defray the expenditure incurred by the Council in the exercise,performance and discharge of its powers and functions under this Act or under any other written law and all such sums as are required to be paid out of the Fund,by this Act.
The financial year of the Council shall be the calendar year.
The provisions of Article 154 of the Constitution relating to the audit of the accounts of public corporations shall apply to the audit of the accounts of the Council.

For the purpose of enabling the Council to exercise and discharge any of the powers and functions under this Act, the Council or any person authorised in that behalf by the Council may by notice in writing require any registered surveyor to furnish to the Council or to the person authorised within such period as shall be specified in the notice, all such returns and information pertaining" to the practice by him, of land surveying as are known to or in the possession of. Such surveyor including original field notes and plans or maps

It shall be the duty of every surveyor who is required to furnish any return or information by a notice under subsection (1), to comply with such requirement within the period specified in such notice, except where he is precluded from making such return or divulging such information under the provisions of any law.

The Council or any member thereof or any officer or servant of the Council, shall not disclose to any person or use any return or information furnished under subsection (i)except when required to do so by a court of law or for the purpose of discharging its functions.
The Council shall be deemed to be a scheduled institution within the meaning of the Bribery Act and the provisions of that Act, shall be construed accordingly.
All members, officers and servants of the Council shall be deemed to be public servants within the meaning and for the purposes of the Penal Code.

Where any immovable property of the State is required for any purpose of the Council, such purpose shall be deemed to be a purpose for which a special grant or lease of such property may be made under section 6 of the State Lands Ordinance and accordingly the provisions of that Ordinance shall apply to a special grant or lease of such property to the Council.

Where any movable property of the State is required for any purpose of the Council, the Minister in charge of the subject of Finance may, by Order published in the Gazette. Transfer to, and vest in the possession and use of such movable property;

provided however, that no order affecting any movable property of the State shall be made by the Minister under the preceding provisions of this subsection. Without the concurrence of the Minister having control over such property.

Where any immovable property is required to be acquired for any specific purpose of the Council and the Minister by Order published in the Gazette approves of the proposed acquisition for that purpose that property shall be deemed to be required for a public purpose and may accordingly be acquired under the Land Acquisition Act and transferred to the Council.
